key_insight: Retention-constrained fine-tuning improves defect predictions in a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential while preserving tested near-equilibrium mechanical and vibrational behavior.
engineering_relevance: The protocol supports more accurate simulations of aluminium defect dynamics and plasticity without sacrificing validated bulk response.
method: Acquire configurations using conditional force uncertainty over 144 readout weights, with within-batch covariance updates.
Iteratively update all model parameters while anchoring protocol-compatible relative energies.
Gate MD–DFT updates against historical elastic-group energy and vibrational tolerances.
evidence_signal: With 32 acquired configurations and 400 gradient updates, mean development force error fell from 22.43 to 21.52 meV/Å, outperforming sampling baselines; all three force-uncertainty runs met retention criteria, with harmonic phonon RMS drift below 0.05 THz.
watch_item: Retention is demonstrated only for the tested bulk responses, and the closed-loop MD–DFT evaluation remains a pilot rather than broad deployment validation.
paper_title: Retention-constrained fine-tuning of a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity
